title: Indian shares snap losing run on IT boost; oil dips after Trump comments
description: June 2 (Reuters) - Indian shares recovered from their lowest levels in nearly two months on Tuesday, led ​by value buying after four straight session of losses and a ‌continued surge in information technology stocks. After a nearly 3% slide over the previous four sessions that was driven by Iran war jitters and unprecedented foreign outflows, the benchmark Nifty 50 (NSEI) ​rose 0.43% to 23,483.55 on Tuesday, while the BSE Sensex (BSESN) gained 0.52% to ​74,649.84.On the day, Indian equities slipped to seventh place globally in ⁠terms of total market capitalisation, with South Korea's chip-heavy listed universe overtaking ​India. U.S. President Donald Trump's comments that talks with Iran are still underway eased nerves ​sparked by an earlier report that Tehran had suspended indirect negotiations with Washington. Brent crude fell 1.3% to $93.7 a barrel, providing a modicum of relief for net energy importer India. Eight of the ​16 major sectors rose, with broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100) and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100) gaining 0.4% and ​0.2%, respectively. "We are seeing value buying as well as sectoral rotation. The momentum is picking ‌up ⁠in IT sector which has been the worst hit this year," said Anita Gandhi, head of institutional business at Arihant Capital Markets. "Markets are still in the midst of uncertainties regarding U.S.-Iran war and a delayed monsoon and will need ​clarity on these ​two fronts for ⁠any further material gains," Gandhi said. "Recent ​commentary from global software companies indicates that rising AI adoption ​is not ⁠only benefitting AI capex and LLM vendors, but also driving demand for software companies," said Sandeep Shah, director of Equirus Securities.
channel: Market Volatility & Investor Confidence
insights: Indian stock indices rebounded on Tuesday, driven by a surge in information technology stocks and value buying after a prolonged losing streak, with the Nifty 50 and Sensex both posting gains. Global market dynamics were influenced by U.S. President Trump’s statements regarding ongoing negotiations with Iran, alleviating earlier concerns about the Iran-U.S. conflict. Brent crude prices decreased, offering some respite to India, a significant energy importer, while sector rotation and small-cap gains further contributed to the positive market movement amidst lingering uncertainties.
summary: This article directly impacts the Indian stock market via a recovery driven by the IT sector and easing of geopolitical tensions (U.S.-Iran talks).
